title: SWITCH and menu choices
outcomes: Choose a suitable multi-way selection structure

sections.heading: One choice several exact values
sections.text: Multi-way selection compares one expression with listed exact values. The idea is often called SWITCH. StudyLab writes CASE choice OF, followed by WHEN 1:, WHEN 2: and OTHERWISE:, then ENDCASE. Use it for exact choices such as menu options. IF is usually clearer for ranges. OTHERWISE handles a choice with no matching WHEN. One matching branch runs without falling into the next branch. Other languages use different syntax.

sections.heading: Before the code
sections.text: Build a tiny menu that displays a course fee. The student enters 1 or 2. Any other integer displays Unknown choice. This example assumes the input has already been converted to an integer. Input conversion and selection are separate responsibilities.

examplePrompt: Input 1 for a R500 SQL course or 2 for a R600 Docker course.
example:
BEGIN
  DECLARE choice AS INTEGER
  INPUT choice
  CASE choice OF
    WHEN 1:
      OUTPUT 500
    WHEN 2:
      OUTPUT 600
    OTHERWISE:
      OUTPUT "Unknown choice"
  ENDCASE
END
exampleTrace: The first branch and OTHERWISE do not run.
choice=3 matches no listed value and displays Unknown choice.
question: Add WHEN 3: for a R700 C# course and explain why OTHERWISE must remain. Test 3 and 0.
answer: Insert WHEN 3: followed by OUTPUT 700 before OTHERWISE:. Choice 3 displays 700. Choice 0 displays Unknown choice. OTHERWISE is still needed because unlisted choices remain possible.

title: Two dimensional arrays and row totals
outcomes: Read and trace a row and column index
Calculate row totals with nested loops

sections.heading: A table of related values
sections.text: A two dimensional array uses two indexes, such as marks[row][column]. The first selects a row and the second selects a column. For two students taking three tests there are 2 * 3 = 6 elements. Zero based row indexes are 0..1 and column indexes are 0..2. A row total must restart at zero for each new student.

sections.heading: Before the code
sections.text: Build a report with one total per student. Student 0 has 50,60,70 and student 1 has 80,40,60. The example assigns all six values before reading them. StudyLab uses separate brackets for each dimension: DECLARE marks[2][3] AS REAL and marks[row][column]. You can test this matrix example in the browser tracer.

examplePrompt: Find each student's total over three tests. Keep the column count separate from the row count.
example:
BEGIN
  DECLARE marks[2][3] AS REAL
  DECLARE row AS INTEGER
  DECLARE column AS INTEGER
  DECLARE rowTotal AS REAL
  SET marks[0][0] = 50
  SET marks[0][1] = 60
  SET marks[0][2] = 70
  SET marks[1][0] = 80
  SET marks[1][1] = 40
  SET marks[1][2] = 60
  FOR row = 0 TO 1
    SET rowTotal = 0 // Restart for this row
    FOR column = 0 TO 2
      SET rowTotal = rowTotal + marks[row][column]
    ENDFOR
    OUTPUT row, rowTotal
  ENDFOR
END
exampleTrace: Row 1 starts again at 0 and totals 80,120,180.
Output pairs are (0,180) and (1,180). The inner body runs six times.
question: Modify the report to display row averages and a total for each column. Give all expected results for the shown data.
answer: Display rowTotal/3.0 after each row loop: 60 and 60. For column totals put the column loop outside a row loop, reset columnTotal before scanning its two rows and accumulate marks[row][column]. Column totals are 130,100,130. Bounds stay rows 0..1 and columns 0..2.

title: Integrated student marks project
outcomes: Combine input validation arrays methods and selection
Plan an independent test set and explain a class design

sections.heading: What you are building
sections.text: Build a marks report for three students. Keep a name and a valid mark for each student. Show each name, mark and result; calculate the class average; find the top student. Use parallel arrays first, then describe how a Student class could keep each name and mark together. The main goal is to make data flow and rules visible.

sections.heading: Build the project in parts
sections.text: Part 1 declares and fills the arrays. Part 2 validates marks from 0 to 100. Part 3 counts passes using mark >= 50. Part 4 calculates the average after all three inputs. Part 5 tracks the best index and prints its matching name. A separate extension moves classification into a returning method. Only read a variable after assigning it.

sections.heading: Testing the whole report
sections.text: Use Ada=50, Bo=49 and Cy=75. Expected average is 58, two students pass and Cy is top. Test all zeros, all hundreds and equal top marks. This design keeps the first top student by using > rather than >=. Reject a negative mark and 101, then enter a replacement. The program accepts exactly three valid records, even if it must ask again.

examplePrompt: The complete main program below combines the parts. Numeric input conversion is assumed; range validation is explicit. Define names and marks before the main report loop.
example:
BEGIN
  DECLARE names[3] AS STRING
  DECLARE marks[3] AS REAL
  DECLARE i AS INTEGER
  DECLARE total AS REAL
  DECLARE passed AS INTEGER
  DECLARE bestIndex AS INTEGER
  SET total = 0
  SET passed = 0
  SET bestIndex = 0

  FOR i = 0 TO 2
    INPUT names[i]
    INPUT marks[i]
    WHILE marks[i] < 0 OR marks[i] > 100 DO
      OUTPUT "Enter a mark from 0 to 100"
      INPUT marks[i]
    ENDWHILE
    SET total = total + marks[i]
    IF marks[i] >= 50 THEN
      SET passed = passed + 1
      OUTPUT names[i], marks[i], "Pass"
    ELSE
      OUTPUT names[i], marks[i], "Revise"
    ENDIF
    IF marks[i] > marks[bestIndex] THEN
      SET bestIndex = i
    ENDIF
  ENDFOR

  OUTPUT "Average", total / 3.0
  OUTPUT "Passed", passed
  OUTPUT "Top", names[bestIndex], marks[bestIndex]
END
question: Refactor the classification into Result(mark) returning a STRING. Give the complete method and the calling statement. Then propose private fields and methods for a Student class.
answer: METHOD Result(mark AS REAL) RETURNS STRING; IF mark >= 50 THEN RETURN "Pass" ELSE RETURN "Revise" ENDIF; ENDMETHOD. Place it outside Main. In the report call OUTPUT names[i],marks[i],Result(marks[i]). Precondition: mark already validated. Student has private name STRING and mark REAL; a constructor checks the mark range, GetName returns the name and Result returns the classification. Keep the main report responsible for aggregation across students.
rubric: Separation of object and class totals
